e-12452.problem: Find the value of the vector function $\mathbf f(t) = \left\langle \cos t, \: \sin t, \: t \right\rangle$ at $t = \pi.$
e-12452.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t = \pi$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\pi ⟩=⟨-1,0,\pi \,⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the value of $\mathbf f (t)$ at $t = \pi$ is $\langle -1, 0, \pi \rangle.$

We can also express the answer using $\mathbf i$-$\mathbf j$-$\mathbf k$ notation or square bracket notation, as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ \pi \end{aligned}]
$$

e-12451.knowledge_point: Finding the Magnitude of a Vector-Valued Function
e-12451.problem: Find $\left|\mathbf r\left(4\right)\right|$ given that $\mathbf r(t)  = \left\langle 2-t, 2\sqrt{t}, \, t-1\right\rangle,$
e-12451.worked_solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(4) & =⟨2-4,\,2\sqrt{4},\,4-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(4)| & =\sqrt{{(-2)}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{29}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Substitute t=π/3. Since cos(5π/3)=1/2 and sin(5π/3)=−√3/2, the components are 6(1/2)=3 and (−√3/2)²=3/4.

$$

$$

after.problem: What is the value of $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{t+2} \\ 5-{t}^{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t-2)\end{aligned}]$ at $t=2?$
after.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=2$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2+2} \\ 5-{2}^{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{4} \\ 5-4 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the value of $f(t)$ at $t=2$ is the vector $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2+2} \\ 5-{2}^{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{4} \\ 5-4 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the value of $f(t)$ at $t=2$ is the vector $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
